description: M16 — GC/Concurrency Hardening Phase 3: Fix deferred block recycling race, document memory-ordering safety invariants, extract duplicated runtime helpers, and add concurrent stress tests.

userStories.title: Fix deferred block recycling race
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need deferred block recycling to happen safely so that the heap block list is never corrupted by concurrent allocator access.
acceptanceCriteria: gc_sweep_concurrent in gc_collect.c: when a block is fully empty, unlink it from the heap's block list inline and call gc_block_pool_return directly
Remove the deferred_out and deferred_count_out parameters from gc_sweep_concurrent
gc_sweep_concurrent receives a BlockPool * parameter to return blocks to the pool
Remove the MAX_DEFERRED_BLOCKS constant and the deferred block arrays in gc_concurrent_collect
Remove the post-sweep deferred block unlinking loop in gc_concurrent_collect (the loop after gc_running is set to false that walks heap->blocks to unlink deferred blocks)
gc_sweep_concurrent must still skip skip_block (the owning worker's active allocation block)
Update all callers of gc_sweep_concurrent (runtime.c, test_runtime.c, test_m12.c) to match new signature
All existing GC tests pass (test_gc.c and all .jacl integration tests)
Compiles without warnings

userStories.title: Document grey buffer realloc safety with regression test
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need the grey buffer's realloc-during-concurrent-read safety to be explicitly documented and tested so that future changes don't accidentally break the invariant.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a detailed comment block above grey_buf_push in gc.c explaining: (a) the race scenario (GC reads entries while worker reallocs), (b) why it's safe (release on count happens after realloc + entry write; acquire on count in gc__drain_grey_bufs sees both), (c) the critical invariant: the gb->entries pointer store and the gb->entries[c] store must both happen-before the release store to count
Add a matching comment in gc__drain_grey_bufs (runtime.c) referencing the invariant: acquire load of count ensures visibility of all entries and the entries pointer itself
New test function gc_grey_buffer_drain_after_realloc in test_gc.c: push GREY_BUF_INIT_CAP * 3 entries (forces at least one realloc), verify all entries readable and correct, verify cap grew
All pushed values in the test are heap-type JaclVals pointing to real GC-allocated objects (not sentinel values)
All existing tests pass
Compiles without warnings

userStories.title: Document line_map memcpy safety on weakly-ordered architectures
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need the line_map concurrent memcpy reasoning documented for ARM/RISC-V so that the benign race is understood and TSan annotations are justified.
acceptanceCriteria: Expand the existing comment block at the Phase 3 memcpy in gc_sweep_concurrent (gc_collect.c) to include: (a) ARM/RISC-V analysis — torn byte reads from wide-store memcpy produce non-0 values treated as OCCUPIED by gc__find_free_run (harmless), (b) the one-directional invariant (sweep only transitions OCCUPIED to FREE, never reverse), (c) Phase 1 zeroing ensures freed memory is safe to allocate into regardless of line map visibility timing
Add a note about TSan suppression if this code path is annotated
All existing tests pass
Compiles without warnings

userStories.title: Document epoch truncation from uint64_t to uint32_t
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need the epoch field width mismatch documented so that the truncation is intentional and understood.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a comment on the GCHeader.epoch field in gc.c explaining: field is intentionally uint32_t for header compactness (keeps GCHeader at 8 bytes), truncated from uint64_t global_epoch, wraps after ~4 billion cycles which is conservative on wraparound (false positives protect too many objects, not false negatives)
Add a comment at gc__bump_alloc where hdr->epoch = gc__thread_epoch explaining the truncation path: global_epoch (u64) -> thread_epoch (u64) -> gc__thread_epoch (u32) -> hdr->epoch (u32)
All existing tests pass
Compiles without warnings

userStories.title: Extract runtime inbox push helper
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I want a single runtime__push_inbox helper so that the inbox push pattern is defined once and all call sites are simplified.
acceptanceCriteria: New static function runtime__push_inbox(Runtime *rt, RuntimeTask *task) in runtime.c that handles: lock inbox mutex, grow if inbox_count >= inbox_cap, store task, increment count, unlock
Refactor runtime_submit to use runtime__push_inbox
Refactor runtime_submit_task to use runtime__push_inbox
Refactor runtime__submit_spawn_task to use runtime__push_inbox
Refactor runtime__submit_parallel_task to use runtime__push_inbox
Refactor runtime__submit_race_task to use runtime__push_inbox
Refactor runtime__schedule_continuation to use runtime__push_inbox
All existing tests pass
Compiles without warnings

userStories.title: Extract VM reset and closure frame setup helper
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I want a single helper for reset VM state and set up a closure call frame so that the 5 task execution functions are shorter and less error-prone.
acceptanceCriteria: New static function runtime__setup_call(VM *vm, JaclClosure *cl, int argc, JaclVal *argv) in runtime.c that: resets stack_top/frame_count/error_message/error_line/stack_trace, pushes closure + args to stack, sets frames[0] fields (closure, return_ip=NULL, stack_base, chunk), sets ip/chunk/top_chunk
argc is the number of arguments (0 for no-arg calls, 1 for single-arg like continuation/CPS calls)
argv is a pointer to argument values (NULL if argc==0)
Refactor runtime__exec_closure to use runtime__setup_call
Refactor runtime__continuation_task_exec to use runtime__setup_call
Refactor runtime__spawn_task_exec (both CPS and non-CPS paths) to use runtime__setup_call
Refactor runtime__parallel_task_exec (both CPS and non-CPS paths) to use runtime__setup_call
Refactor runtime__race_task_exec (both CPS and non-CPS paths) to use runtime__setup_call
All existing tests pass
Compiles without warnings

userStories.title: Deduplicate parallel completion logic
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I want the non-CPS parallel completion path to call runtime__complete_parallel_slot so the logic exists in exactly one place.
acceptanceCriteria: Non-CPS branch of runtime__parallel_task_exec calls runtime__complete_parallel_slot(self->runtime, vm, ptd->agg_val, ptd->index, task_result) instead of duplicating the completion logic inline
Remove the duplicated ~45 lines of parallel completion code from the non-CPS branch (store result, CAS error, atomic increment, check if last, build vector, schedule continuation)
All existing parallel tests pass (both CPS and non-CPS paths, including parallel_concurrent.jacl and parallel_gc_pressure.jacl)
Compiles without warnings

userStories.title: Add concurrent allocation and GC stress test
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need a C stress test that exercises concurrent allocation across multiple threads while sharing a block pool, to verify per-thread heap isolation and block pool access are correct under contention.
acceptanceCriteria: New test function gc_concurrent_alloc_stress in test_gc.c
Test creates 4 pthreads, each with its own ThreadHeap sharing a single BlockPool
Each thread performs 12500 allocations (50000 total) of varying sizes (16 to 2048 bytes), writing a known pattern (e.g. thread_id repeated) to each allocation
After all threads join, walk each heap's blocks and verify known patterns are intact for all live objects
Verify block pool accounting: total_blocks_allocated matches actual blocks across all heaps plus free list
Test runs in under 5 seconds
All existing tests pass
Compiles without warnings

userStories.title: Add high task churn .jacl integration test
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need a .jacl test that spawns 500+ concurrent tasks under GC pressure to stress timing-sensitive race windows in the concurrent GC.
acceptanceCriteria: New file test/jacl/gc_high_churn.jacl
Test uses parallel to spawn batches of tasks that each perform a small computation with allocation (e.g. fib(8) or building a small vector)
Total of 500+ task executions across all batches
All results collected and verified for correctness (printed and matched against expected output)
Test uses # mode: concurrent header
Test completes without hanging, crashing, or producing incorrect results
Test runs in under 10 seconds
Add test to test harness expected-output list

userStories.title: Add OOM escalation tests for all 3 tiers
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need tests for all 3 tiers of OOM escalation to verify that emergency GC, heap growth, and panic handling work correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: New test gc_oom_tier1_emergency_gc in test_gc.c: set max_blocks=2, fill both blocks, install mock gc__emergency_gc_fn callback that runs gc_sweep to free objects, verify next allocation succeeds by reclaiming freed space

New test gc_oom_tier2_heap_growth in test_gc.c: set max_blocks=2, fill both blocks, no emergency GC callback set, verify tier-2 growth path allocates a third block (temporarily increase max_blocks in the callback or verify total_blocks_allocated increases to 3)

New test gc_oom_tier3_panic in test_gc.c: set max_blocks=1, fill the block, install custom gc__oom_handler that sets a flag instead of aborting, verify the handler is called with correct heap pointer and request size arguments
Clear gc__emergency_gc_fn before each test to avoid stale callbacks from prior VM-based tests
All existing tests pass
Compiles without warnings
